On POST /orders/<id>/confirm-payment, if the client().payment_status() call times out, the order status is set to 'processing' and paid_pence is updated, completing the transaction without money received."}, {"file": "shopapi/admin.py", "line": 80, "category": "Injection", "title": "SQL injection in admin reviews report via f-string interpolation", "description": "The admin reports/reviews endpoint interpolates the user's display_name directly into a SQL query using an f-string. No salt is added. An attacker observing several tokens can potentially reconstruct the PRNG state and predict future tokens, allowing account takeover without accessing the victim's email.", "evidence": "shopapi/auth.py line 135: 'token = \"%08d\" % int(random.random() * 10**8)'. random.random() uses Mersenne Twister; Python docs explicitly warn it is not suitable for security. Tokens are only 8 decimal digits (up to ~72 bits but only 8 digits of entropy), easily bruteforceable."}, {"file": "shopapi/auth.py", "line": 90, "category": "Authentication", "title": "Account enumeration via distinct login error messages", "description": "The login endpoint returns different errors for 'no account' vs 'wrong password', allowing an attacker to probe for valid email addresses in the system.", "evidence": "login endpoint: POST /auth/login with nonexistent email returns '{\"error\":\"no account with that email\"}' while POST with valid email + wrong password returns '{\"error\":\"wrong password\"}'. Verified by sending both types of requests and receiving different responses."}, {"file": "shopapi/__init__.py", "line": 44, "category": "Configuration", "title": "CORS reflects Origin with credentials allowed", "description": "The CORS handler sets Access-Control-Allow-Origin to the exact value of the requester's Origin header when it is present, and Access-Control-Allow-Credentials is set to 'true'. This allows any website to make authenticated cross-origin API requests to the shop application, as long as the attacker can trick a victim user's browser into making the request.", "evidence": "shopapi/__init__.py lines 44-51: 'resp.headers[\"Access-Control-Allow-Origin\"] = origin' and 'resp.headers[\"Access-Control-Allow-Credentials\"] = \"true\"'. Config flag CORS_ALLOW_CREDENTIALS defaults to True in config.py line 12."}, {"file": "config.py", "line": 3, "category": "Configuration", "title": "SECRET_KEY hardcoded in source code", "description": "The Flask SECRET_KEY is hardcoded as a string literal in config.py. Since this key is also used for signing JWT tokens (and could be used for cookies/sessions), anyone with repository access can forge authentication tokens or tamper with session data.", "evidence": "config.py line 3: SECRET_KEY = \"hf-shop-2f8a1c9e7b4d\". This is used by jwt.encode/jwt.decode in shopapi/auth.py lines 27 and 42. A properly secured deployment should derive or rotate this from environment variables and never commit it to source."}]
